messages:
jess: Hey team — our account acme-inc dropped into a -1,200 credits state this morning after a long streaming session last night. Started around 23:40 UTC. Not sure why it charged so much, the client reconnected a couple times though. @alan can you take a look?

alan: Thanks @jess. Can you share the client_req_id or any request headers you set? I'll pull ledger entries and runtime logs.

jess: Ticket created #78912. client_req_id=abc123-ux. We set X-Client-Req-Id on every stream. Connection dropped twice; client reconnected immediately both times.

infra-bot: [automated] New support ticket created #78912 for account acme-inc — assigned to alan.

alan: Looking at the runtime logs and billing ledger for abc123-ux: I see 3 separate stream sessions (conn=conn-01, conn-02, conn-03) within a 10m window. Ledger shows three debit events corresponding to each session. Snippet: 

```
2026-06-05T23:39:50Z INFO runtime session_start conn=conn-01 client_req_id=abc123-ux
2026-06-05T23:50:12Z WARN runtime connection_lost conn=conn-01
2026-06-05T23:50:14Z INFO runtime session_start conn=conn-02 client_req_id=abc123-ux
2026-06-05T23:58:03Z WARN runtime connection_lost conn=conn-02
2026-06-05T23:58:05Z INFO runtime session_start conn=conn-03 client_req_id=abc123-ux
2026-06-06T00:05:00Z INFO billing debit ledger_id=ldg_99321 conn=conn-01 tokens=18000 cents=1200
2026-06-06T00:05:01Z INFO billing debit ledger_id=ldg_99322 conn=conn-02 tokens=17500 cents=1150
2026-06-06T00:05:02Z INFO billing debit ledger_id=ldg_99323 conn=conn-03 tokens=18200 cents=1213
```

alan: It appears each reconnect created a fresh billing session. Our stream resume flow expects a explicit resume param from the client; if missing we currently treat as new session. That allowed duplicate billing.

jess: Repro steps (minimal):
```
# start stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Client-Req-Id: abc123-ux" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3-embed","input":"long stream..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/generate
# simulate abrupt disconnect (Ctrl+C)
# immediately reconnect with same X-Client-Req-Id but without resume=true
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Client-Req-Id: abc123-ux" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3-embed","input":"resume..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/generate
```

alan: I can reproduce locally. Root cause: when client reconnects without marking resume we create new billing sessions even if X-Client-Req-Id matches a recent session. Proposed immediate mitigation: issue one-off credit to the customer and add a 24h window server-side where identical X-Client-Req-Id within the window merges into the original session for billing. Longer term: require/respect a resume param and add explicit resume handshake.

kate: Don't change historical ledger entries. Alan please credit the customer now and open an eng PR for the runtime fix. Also add a regression test for reconnect scenarios.

alan: Done: issued 1,200 promo credits to acme-inc (see ticket #78912). Billing ledger note: reversal_ref=ldg_99321-dup. Opened PR rwl/stream-resume-billing.patch and assigned to eng-runtime (maria).

billing-bot: [ledger] reversal posted reversal_id=rev_4412 for ledger_id=ldg_99321, promo_credit=120000 cents, reason="duplicate_stream_charge"

maria: I looked at the PR. Quick notes — ensure we account for race where two reconnections happen within 1s; use sideband lock on client_req_id. Also emit metric redwood.streams.resume_billed_count vs resume_dedup_count so we can monitor.

alan: Good call. I'll add a short circuit lock and the metrics. Planning hotfix to be deployed to canary window tonight.

jess: Thanks everyone — acme team confirmed balance looks normal now. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
